comments.author: @UnseenWorldDocs_Us
comments.text: The part about Bhutan lifting its tobacco ban during the pandemic surprised me, shows they'll change rules when needed. I'm curious how the new Gelephu Mindfulness City will keep jobs for young people without losing the old customs. I'd love to see how they cook meals in places like Bumthang while the cranes gather in the valley.

comments.author: @GlobalLifeInsights
comments.text: Question for everyone watching: If your country decided to measure success by happiness instead of GDP like Bhutan did, do you think people would actually trust the system? Drop your thoughts below!

replies.author: @Globallife.documentary
replies.text: Honestly, most people wouldn’t trust it at first—after decades of being judged by paychecks and GDP numbers, a government handing out "happiness scores" would feel like pure PR unless it actually came with real free healthcare, education, and breathing room like in Bhutan.

comments.author: @Sportinglogic
comments.text: The will to measure everything is a modern feature and modernity is a Western European cultural by-product with which other countries are co-opted as China is today.

replies.author: @Globallife.documentary
replies.text: What an insightful critique! Even when Bhutan set out to reject Western GDP logic, it still ended up using a modern metric-driven ledger to prove its worth—which really captures how inescapable that impulse to measure everything has become globally.
